reason: A is the better, though still under-specified, proposal because coherent nanoscale precipitation is a physically plausible single mediator for improving high-temperature strength and creep resistance, with a direct treated-versus-control falsification test. B is weakened by the unsupported claim that solutionizing, quenching, and aging will refine grains—and by invoking Hall–Petch strengthening at 700–1000 °C, where fine grains can instead accelerate grain-boundary-mediated creep—while its γ′ concept largely repeats the cited prior work.
